Topic1.Title: Public Participation: South Boulder Rec Center and Tipped Wage Concerns
Topic1.Summary: Nineteen speakers addressed council during open comment, with many urging council to preserve the South Boulder Rec Center and its pool, citing health, youth, and accessibility benefits. Several speakers opposed freezing or reducing the tipped wage credit, arguing it would harm workers already living paycheck to paycheck. Other speakers raised concerns about open space tax changes, bear conflict policy, and Palestine-related issues. Council members thanked the speakers, particularly the young people, and encouraged public participation in the Fund Our Future process.

Topic2.Title: Arts Week Declaration
Topic2.Summary: Council Member Benjamin presented a declaration recognizing April 3 through April 12, 2026 as Boulder Arts Week. The declaration highlighted Boulder's creative economy, including its ranking for artist concentration and substantial arts-related economic activity. Dr. Nicholas Felder, this year's Bright Futures Award recipient, accepted the declaration and spoke about the role of art in community identity.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 4A through 4Q unanimously, with Council Member Adams voting no on item 4H regarding Area 3 service area expansion. Item 4F, a 10-year water lease agreement with the Town of Erie, was discussed and staff explained that the minimal lease amount does not jeopardize Boulder's water supply. Staff also noted the battery storage sales tax timing would be immediate.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed call-up items including a Boulder Jewish Commons synagogue site review, a Left Hand Water District request, a student housing development at 1128 28th Street and 2895 East College Avenue, and a landmark alteration certificate on Concord Avenue. A motion to call up the student housing project for Design Advisory Board referral was withdrawn after staff confirmed DAB had already reviewed it unanimously. No other items were called up.

Topic5.Title: Public Hearing: Festival Lodging Rental Ordinance (Ordinance 8743)
Topic5.Summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted Ordinance 8743 to allow tenants and owners of long-term rentals to apply for festival lodging rental licenses for Sundance Film Festival housing. The ordinance creates a new one-year, $75 license tier, requires owner consent for tenant participation, and does not regulate revenue splits between landlords and tenants. Speakers from Barha supported an additional option allowing vacant-unit-only participation, which council did not adopt, while others supported the ordinance as written. The ordinance passed 8 to 0.

Topic6.Title: Matters from the City Manager: Exploring Authority to Modify the Tip Offset
Topic6.Summary: Staff presented the new local authority to modify the tipped wage credit, which Colorado allows jurisdictions with a higher minimum wage to adjust, and outlined four options ranging from status quo to maximizing the tip offset. Restaurant sales and employment data were discussed, with corrections noted for sales tax trends and job figures. Council straw polls kept the status quo, Options 2A, 2B, and Council Member Benjamin's proposed freeze with sunset on the table, while removing the maximized tip offset. Council also directed staff to work with CAC on scheduling a delayed public hearing to allow more data and student participation.
